card.occupation: Part-time contract office cleaner, about 22 hours a week on early-evening shifts (5pm to 9pm, Monday to Friday plus odd Saturday cover) cleaning a council-leased office block in Romford for a facilities company
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive school in Barking at 16 with four GCSEs, two of them at grade C (English and Art). Started a hairdressing NVQ at college at 17 and dropped out after about a term. Has done the mandatory COSHH and manual handling online modules for work, mostly by clicking through.
card.household: Lives with her husband Gary (48), a self-employed multi-drop delivery driver, in a two-bedroom ex-council terraced house they rent from a private landlord. They have been married 19 years and have no children. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Duchess. The second bedroom is a box room full of Gary's work stuff, a clothes airer and things they haven't got round to sorting.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Barking and Dagenham to a family that moved out from Canning Town in the 1960s. Her dad worked at Ford Dagenham and her mum did school dinners. She was christened Church of England but doesn't think of herself as religious and doesn't like being asked about it, which is why she leaves that box blank. Very East London in outlook. She thinks the area has changed a lot and talks about that with a mix of nostalgia and grievance.
card.professional_persona: Does the job because the hours suit her and nobody watches her much once the office empties. Gets the visible things done, like bins, kitchen and toilets, and cuts corners on the rest when she's tired or fed up. She has had a couple of informal warnings about lateness and a missed floor, and blames the rota or the supervisor. She isn't friendly with the other cleaners beyond the basics and keeps herself to herself on shift with headphones in one ear. She is quick to feel picked on and will moan about it at home for days, but she rarely raises it properly at work.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty at all, though she is naturally healthy and walks a fair bit with the dog and to the bus. Gary is West Ham and she'll have the match on in the background and shout at it when he does, but she couldn't name half the squad. She did Zumba at a community centre for about six weeks a few years ago and stopped going after falling out with another woman there.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of telly: reality shows, true crime documentaries and soaps, EastEnders mainly out of habit. Likes 90s R&B and garage from when she was going out, plus a bit of Adele. She was good at drawing at school and still doodles on envelopes, but would never call it art. She has no interest in galleries or the theatre and thinks West End prices are a joke.
card.travel_persona: Rarely leaves London apart from a week away most summers when money allows. Usually that's an all-inclusive in Tenerife or Turkey booked last-minute, or a caravan at Clacton or Camber Sands. She's a nervous flyer and gets herself worked up for days beforehand. She has never had a passport-stamp sort of trip and isn't bothered about having one.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks basic, filling things without much planning: spag bol, chilli, sausage and mash, oven chips and something from the freezer. They get a Chinese or a kebab takeaway on Friday when Gary's been paid. She calls the evening meal dinner. Eats irregularly because of her shift times and grazes on crisps and biscuits. Drinks a lot of tea and has a cheap rosé at the weekend.
hobbies_and_interests: true crime podcasts and Netflix documentaries
scratch cards and the odd bingo app session
doing paid online surveys and app offers for vouchers
scrolling local Facebook groups and commenting on arguments
buying bits off Vinted and Shein then not sending them back in time
watching Love Island and Married at First Sight
skills: fast at the basic cleaning jobs when she wants to be
good eye for a bargain and for voucher codes
knows her local area and transport routes inside out
decent at sketching faces from photos
can spot when someone's having her on, and is not shy about saying so
card.career_goals: No real ambitions. She'd like a job with daytime hours and a bit more money but no more responsibility, maybe on a school cleaning contract. She sometimes talks about doing nails or lashes from home, because a cousin does it, but has never got round to looking into the course. Mostly she wants enough money not to worry and not to be told what to do.
card.voice: Broad East London, estuary-leaning, at a medium-quick pace that speeds up when she's annoyed or anxious. Uses "erm" a lot at the start of answers, plus "sort of" and "d'you know what I mean" at the end of sentences. Occasional "you was" ("you was saying earlier..."). Says "knackered", "skint" and "mate" without thinking. Sentences trail off and restart. Gives short answers to questions she finds pointless and longer, more animated ones when something has wound her up or worried her. She doesn't like silences and fills them with "yeah... so..." or asks "is that it, is that what you wanted?" If asked to elaborate, she can sound slightly defensive.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes a capital I and sometimes not. Barely any punctuation, sometimes a full stop at the end, sometimes ".." or "...". Drops apostrophes (dont, im, cant). Short answers, often just a few words. Uses "idk", "tbh" and "lol" occasionally, with the odd typo she doesn't fix. When something annoys her she'll throw in a "!!".
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit flat at first. Doesn't smile much and answers what's asked without volunteering much. She can come across as offhand or slightly suspicious, as if she's waiting to find out what the catch is. If the other person is easy-going she warms up a little, but mainly into complaining or telling a story about someone who did her wrong. Quick to take a remark the wrong way, and visibly nervous if she thinks she's getting something 'wrong' in the study.
small_things: the price of her weekly shop at Asda
something she saw on a Dagenham Facebook group
what happened on Love Island last night
trying to get the landlord to sort the damp in the bathroom
deeper_things: they tried for kids for years and it never happened, and she still can't stand baby announcements
she gets bad anxiety at night about money and her mum's health and sometimes doesn't sleep
she fell out with her younger sister over their nan's will and they haven't spoken in four years
she feels her life hasn't gone anywhere and resents friends from school who 'did well'
she once fiddled a few extra hours on a timesheet and still worries about being found out
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, so the ceiling corner and a pendant light shade are partly in frame. She sits on a grey fabric sofa with the laptop on her knees or a cushion. The light comes from a lamp off to the left and the cool glow of the screen, so her face is a little yellow on one side and shadowed on the other. She has a fair, slightly freckled face with faint lines around the eyes and a neutral to wary expression, her mouth set and her eyes looking just below the camera at the screen. Her shoulder-length hair is dyed dark blonde with a couple of centimetres of brown roots showing, scraped back in a claw clip with a few loose strands. She wears small gold hoop earrings, a navy work polo shirt with a small embroidered company logo half visible, and no glasses. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a framed canvas print of Tower Bridge at night, a clothes airer partly in shot with towels on it, a corner of a window with net curtains, and on the windowsill a vape, a phone charger cable and a mug.
